title: Password Reset: Passwords & 2FA

freshness.note: options reused from security-ready-1 (split, not new)

pairs.ask: Keep The Password Manager Emergency Kit Offline: Do It Or Not Now?

optionA.label: Do It
optionA.desc: Export the password manager emergency kit and keep it offline with your recovery codes. Who does it: You.

visual.svg: <svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" viewBox="0 0 240 300" width="240" height="300" style="max-width:100%;height:auto"><rect width="240" height="300" rx="14" fill="#FFFFFF" stroke="#E5E0D8"/><rect x="0" y="0" width="240" height="8" rx="4" fill="#16a34a"/><text x="18" y="30" font-size="9" fill="#525252" font-family="Hind" font-weight="600">SECURITY</text><text x="18" y="58" font-size="17" fill="#0A0A0A" font-family="Khand" font-weight="700">Do It</text><text x="18" y="108" font-size="10.5" fill="#262626" font-family="Hind" font-weight="400">Export the password manager emergency</text><text x="18" y="123" font-size="10.5" fill="#262626" font-family="Hind" font-weight="400">kit and keep it offline with your</text><text x="18" y="138" font-size="10.5" fill="#262626" font-family="Hind" font-weight="400">recovery codes. Who does it: You.</text></svg>

optionB.label: Not Now
optionB.desc: Leave it for now. Why it matters: If the password manager login is lost, every stored password is lost with it.

visual.svg: <svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" viewBox="0 0 240 300" width="240" height="300" style="max-width:100%;height:auto"><rect width="240" height="300" rx="14" fill="#FFFFFF" stroke="#E5E0D8"/><rect x="0" y="0" width="240" height="8" rx="4" fill="#A3A3A3"/><text x="18" y="30" font-size="9" fill="#525252" font-family="Hind" font-weight="600">SECURITY</text><text x="18" y="58" font-size="17" fill="#0A0A0A" font-family="Khand" font-weight="700">Not Now</text><text x="18" y="108" font-size="10.5" fill="#262626" font-family="Hind" font-weight="400">Leave it for now. Why it matters: If</text><text x="18" y="123" font-size="10.5" fill="#262626" font-family="Hind" font-weight="400">the password manager login is lost,</text><text x="18" y="138" font-size="10.5" fill="#262626" font-family="Hind" font-weight="400">every stored password is lost with it.</text></svg>

pairs.ask: Monthly Scan For Plain-Text Passwords: Do It Or Not Now?

optionA.label: Do It
optionA.desc: Each month Security searches the shared computer for plain-text passwords and tokens and replaces them with a pointer to the vault. Who does it: Security.

visual.svg: <svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" viewBox="0 0 240 300" width="240" height="300" style="max-width:100%;height:auto"><rect width="240" height="300" rx="14" fill="#FFFFFF" stroke="#E5E0D8"/><rect x="0" y="0" width="240" height="8" rx="4" fill="#16a34a"/><text x="18" y="30" font-size="9" fill="#525252" font-family="Hind" font-weight="600">SECURITY</text><text x="18" y="58" font-size="17" fill="#0A0A0A" font-family="Khand" font-weight="700">Do It</text><text x="18" y="108" font-size="10.5" fill="#262626" font-family="Hind" font-weight="400">Each month Security searches the</text><text x="18" y="123" font-size="10.5" fill="#262626" font-family="Hind" font-weight="400">shared computer for plain-text</text><text x="18" y="138" font-size="10.5" fill="#262626" font-family="Hind" font-weight="400">passwords and tokens and replaces them</text><text x="18" y="153" font-size="10.5" fill="#262626" font-family="Hind" font-weight="400">with a pointer to the vault. Who does</text><text x="18" y="168" font-size="10.5" fill="#262626" font-family="Hind" font-weight="400">it: Security.</text></svg>

optionB.label: Not Now
optionB.desc: Leave it for now. Why it matters: Passwords were found in plain text in shared files and scrubbed. New ones can creep back in.

visual.svg: <svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" viewBox="0 0 240 300" width="240" height="300" style="max-width:100%;height:auto"><rect width="240" height="300" rx="14" fill="#FFFFFF" stroke="#E5E0D8"/><rect x="0" y="0" width="240" height="8" rx="4" fill="#A3A3A3"/><text x="18" y="30" font-size="9" fill="#525252" font-family="Hind" font-weight="600">SECURITY</text><text x="18" y="58" font-size="17" fill="#0A0A0A" font-family="Khand" font-weight="700">Not Now</text><text x="18" y="108" font-size="10.5" fill="#262626" font-family="Hind" font-weight="400">Leave it for now. Why it matters:</text><text x="18" y="123" font-size="10.5" fill="#262626" font-family="Hind" font-weight="400">Passwords were found in plain text in</text><text x="18" y="138" font-size="10.5" fill="#262626" font-family="Hind" font-weight="400">shared files and scrubbed. New ones</text><text x="18" y="153" font-size="10.5" fill="#262626" font-family="Hind" font-weight="400">can creep back in.</text></svg>

pairs.ask: Passkey On Your Main Google Account First: Do It Or Not Now?

optionA.label: Do It
optionA.desc: Security walks you through adding a passkey to your main Google account on your phone; you tap Approve. Who does it: You, With Security.

optionB.label: Not Now
optionB.desc: Leave it for now. Why it matters: Google is the reset address for most of your other accounts, so it is the first one to protect.

pairs.ask: Authenticator App On GitHub: Do It Or Not Now?

optionA.label: Do It
optionA.desc: Turn on an authenticator app for the WebermanApps GitHub login and save its recovery codes in 1Password. Who does it: You, With Security.

optionB.label: Not Now
optionB.desc: Leave it for now. Why it matters: GitHub holds all 45 sites and their history. One stolen password could change or delete them.

pairs.ask: 2FA On The Netlify Account: Do It Or Not Now?

optionA.desc: Turn on 2FA for the Netlify account that still hosts the three old public copies. Who does it: You, With Security.

pairs.ask: One Shared 1Password Vault For Agent Logins: Do It Or Not Now?

optionA.label: Do It
optionA.desc: Security makes an Agents vault in 1Password for the logins agents use, so they stop living in notes and files. You keep admin. Who does it: Security.

visual.svg: <svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" viewBox="0 0 240 300" width="240" height="300" style="max-width:100%;height:auto"><rect width="240" height="300" rx="14" fill="#FFFFFF" stroke="#E5E0D8"/><rect x="0" y="0" width="240" height="8" rx="4" fill="#16a34a"/><text x="18" y="30" font-size="9" fill="#525252" font-family="Hind" font-weight="600">SECURITY</text><text x="18" y="58" font-size="17" fill="#0A0A0A" font-family="Khand" font-weight="700">Do It</text><text x="18" y="108" font-size="10.5" fill="#262626" font-family="Hind" font-weight="400">Security makes an Agents vault in</text><text x="18" y="123" font-size="10.5" fill="#262626" font-family="Hind" font-weight="400">1Password for the logins agents use,</text><text x="18" y="138" font-size="10.5" fill="#262626" font-family="Hind" font-weight="400">so they stop living in notes and</text><text x="18" y="153" font-size="10.5" fill="#262626" font-family="Hind" font-weight="400">files. You keep admin. Who does it:</text><text x="18" y="168" font-size="10.5" fill="#262626" font-family="Hind" font-weight="400">Security.</text></svg>

optionB.label: Not Now
optionB.desc: Leave it for now. Why it matters: Today agent logins sit in shared files. One vault with an owner is easier to rotate and audit.

pairs.ask: Monthly 1Password Watchtower Check: Do It Or Not Now?

optionA.label: Do It
optionA.desc: Once a month Security reads the 1Password Watchtower list (reused, weak or breached passwords) and puts the top 3 fixes in the Morning Report. Who does it: Security.

optionB.label: Not Now

pairs.ask: Keep The Page Password Only In 1Password: Do It Or Not Now?

optionA.label: Do It
optionA.desc: Save the shared page password in 1Password and remove it from chats and notes, so it lives in one place. Who does it: You, With Security.

optionB.label: Not Now
optionB.desc: Leave it for now. Why it matters: The same password opens all 45 sites, so every extra copy is one more place it can leak.
